statement: There exists a predicate P on C={0,1} and A={0,1} such that (forall c in C)(exists A in A) P(c,A), but not (exists A in A)(forall c in C) P(c,A). Take P(c,A) iff A=c.
proof: For each c in {0,1}, choose A=c, proving the first statement. For the second, any fixed A in {0,1} fails P(c,A) at the other element c=1-A. Thus no A works for every c.

statement: Assuming MMW19 Theorem 1.2, for every oracle A and time-constructible s(n) >= n, search-MCSP^A[s(n)] has a one-pass algorithm using poly(s) space and update time, with Sigma_3 SAT^A queries of O~(s)-bit length. Therefore no lower bound can exclude every algorithm in an augmented streaming model permitting these transitions. By PH nesting, the same holds for Sigma_k SAT^A-oracle models for each fixed k >= 3.
proof: MMW19 Theorem 1.2 supplies, for every such A and s, a correct one-pass algorithm with O~(s) space, O~(s^2) update time, and Sigma_3 SAT^A queries of length O~(s). These bounds are polynomial in s, so the algorithm belongs to the augmented model. For fixed k >= 3, Sigma_3^A predicates are contained in Sigma_k^A by padding the quantifier prefix with dummy blocks. Thus an alleged lower bound excluding every algorithm in the augmented model contradicts this algorithm. This argument makes no claim for k < 3 or for stricter resource or query-length bounds.

statement: Assume the exact hypotheses and conclusion of MMW19 Theorem 1.2. For every fixed k≥3, an augmented one-pass streaming model that permits Σ_k^A-SAT oracle queries of length at least the theorem’s O~(s(n)) bound, and allows at least its O~(s(n)^2) update time and O~(s(n)) space, cannot have a lower bound excluding all algorithms for search-MCSP^A[s(n)].
proof: Fix any oracle A and any time-constructible s(n)≥n covered by Theorem 1.2. That theorem supplies a correct one-pass search-MCSP^A[s(n)] algorithm using a Σ_3 SAT^A oracle, O~(s(n)) query length, O~(s(n)^2) update time, and O~(s(n)) space. For fixed k≥3, Σ_3^A predicates are expressible in Σ_k^A by adding dummy quantifier blocks, so the same algorithm is allowed in the stated augmented model. Its resource bounds meet that model’s allowances. Therefore a lower bound excluding every algorithm in that model would exclude this algorithm, contradicting the theorem. This implication is conditional on the cited theorem and says nothing about k<3 or models with tighter query or resource limits.

statement: Let k≥0 be fixed. Suppose R(c,x) is a uniformly specified predicate in Σ_k^P, with c and x given as inputs and one polynomial bound applying to all inputs. Define A* = {⟨c,x⟩ : R(c,x)} and A_c = {x : R(c,x)}. Then A*∈Σ_k^P and A_c={x:⟨c,x⟩∈A*} for every c.
proof: By definition, membership in A* is decided by the same Σ_k^P predicate R on input ⟨c,x⟩, so A*∈Σ_k^P under the stated uniform polynomial bound. For each fixed c, the section of A* obtained by fixing the first coordinate to c is exactly {x:R(c,x)}=A_c. The encoding map x↦⟨c,x⟩ is polynomial-time for each fixed c. Hence the family is represented by one oracle, with each member recovered by tagged queries. This statement concerns oracle membership and does not assert that any separate lower-bound property P(c,A_c) transfers to P(c,A*).

lemma: LEMMA (tagged-oracle simulation with query-cost bound). Let C be a finite set with an injective encoding enc_C of length b bits. Let R(c,x) define A_c={x:R(c,x)} and A*={(enc_C(c),x):R(c,x)}. Any deterministic algorithm making q queries to A_c, each of length at most L, can be simulated with A* using exactly q queries of length at most b+L+O(1), by replacing each x-query with (enc_C(c),x). The simulation preserves the answer sequence, internal transitions, and output. Proof: For each query x, the definition of A* gives A*((enc_C(c),x))=1 iff R(c,x), iff A_c(x)=1. Thus each answer agrees. Induction over the query sequence gives identical configurations and output. The tag and fixed delimiter/length encoding add b+O(1) bits. This makes no claim about the cost of computing R or enc_C, nor about transfer of a lower-bound property.
